scenes.text: Charles Darwin's most famous book sold out on the very first day.
On the Origin of Species came out in London in November eighteen fifty nine.
All one thousand two hundred and fifty copies of the first printing sold in a day.
Years earlier, Darwin had sailed on HMS Beagle for nearly five years, starting in eighteen thirty one.
The key idea came to him in eighteen thirty eight, after reading Thomas Malthus.
Then in eighteen fifty eight, a letter arrived from a naturalist named Alfred Russel Wallace.
Wallace had worked out almost the same theory on his own.
Their papers were read together at the Linnean Society that same year.
The Origin's only illustration is a branching diagram, an early tree of life.
It was hugely controversial, and Thomas Henry Huxley became its fierce defender.
Today there are more than two hundred fifty English editions, plus translations in at least twenty nine languages.
Would you have believed Darwin back in eighteen fifty nine?

title: Darwin's famous book sold out in ONE day 📚
caption: On the Origin of Species was published in London in November 1859, and all 1,250 copies of the first printing sold in a day. Darwin had sat on the idea for about 20 years.
